title: The strict quotient-tower exchange realizes the completed-adjunction mate
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $I\subset A$ an ideal [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and assume that $P_n=A/I^n$ is perfect over $A$ for every $n\geq1$, meaning quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $A$-modules. Let $X,Y,X',Y'$ be small sites [def-weil-size-convention], with a commutative square of their topoi having edges $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$ and a specified isomorphism $fg'\cong gf'$. Use constant $A$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], exact module inverse images $u^*$ and canonical derived adjunctions $u^*\dashv Ru_*$. Put $C_T(M)=R\lim_n(M\otimes_A^L\underline{P_n}_T)$, with the completion unit and completed adjunctions of [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]. Denote the derived-complete subcategory there by $D_{\mathrm{comp}}(T,A)$ and set $u_c^*=C_Uu^*$ for an edge $u:U\to V$.

Let $\mathcal T_T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$, the strict inverse-sequence category [def-weil-inverse-system], realized on the diagram site [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Use its total derived inverse limit $\mathcal L_T=R\lim$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Write $G_u=u^*$ termwise and $R_u^{\mathcal T}$ for the derived termwise direct image. Let $\mathcal R_T(M)=\Delta M\otimes^L_{\Delta\underline A_T}(\underline{P_n}_T)_n$ on this diagram site; equivalently it is represented by a single flat-term K-flat representative $Q\to M$ and the strict quotient diagram $(Q\otimes_A\underline{P_n})_n$ [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For $K\in D_{\mathrm{comp}}(X,A)$ define
$$B=G_gR_f^{\mathcal T}\mathcal R_XK,\qquad D=R_{f'}^{\mathcal T}G_{g'}\mathcal R_XK.$$
Let $E^{\mathcal T}:G_gR_f^{\mathcal T}\to R_{f'}^{\mathcal T}G_{g'}$ be the mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of the termwise pullback square, and put $v=E^{\mathcal T}_{\mathcal R_XK}:B\to D$.

Define $H:\mathcal R_{Y'}(g^*Rf_*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ to be $G_g$ of the diagram-site projection-formula map for $f$ and the quotient diagram, after the canonical pullback/tensor identification. The projection-formula map is the adjunct of counit tensored with the identity [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence], and uses the canonical derived tensor/pullback comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Define
$$s:g_c^*Rf_*K=C_{Y'}(g^*Rf_*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_{Y'}\mathcal R_{Y'}(g^*Rf_*K)\xrightarrow{\mathcal L_{Y'}H}\mathcal L_{Y'}B.$$
The displayed $H$ is invertible; its evaluation at $n$ is the canonical projection-formula isomorphism for the constant perfect coefficient complex $\underline{P_n}$. Let
$$t:Rf'_*g_c'^*K=Rf'_*\mathcal L_{X'}G_{g'}\mathcal R_XK\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_{Y'}D$$
be the canonical derived-direct-image/derived-limit comparison, computed on a K-injective tower and normalized so its projections are the direct images of that tower's projections [def-pur-kinjective-complex].

Let $E^c:g_c^*Rf_*K\to Rf'_*g_c'^*K$ be the mate for the completed adjunctions of the pullback square $f_c'^*g_c^*\cong g_c'^*f_c^*$. The completed pullback composition maps here are the adjunction conjugates [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] of the canonical direct-image composition maps, so their units and counits have fixed normalization. Then
$$t\circ E^c=\mathcal L_{Y'}(v)\circ s.$$
The equality holds as a natural-transformation equality, with these specified comparison maps; it is not a criterion using equality of evaluated tower morphisms. Under the canonical finite coefficient restriction comparisons, evaluating $v$ at $n$ is the ordinary $P_n$-coefficient adjunction mate. No properness, smoothness, constructibility, or etale-origin hypothesis is imposed on this square or on $K$.

proof.text: Represent the ordinary reduction/pullback and finite scalar-extension/pullback comparisons as explicit squares of iterated complex functors. Insert the explicit finite quotient evaluation comparison in the finite normalization. These are the same degreewise maps: the complex square hom formula identifies the former with NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex, and quotient evaluation is the identity in each degree. Thus the representative normalizations and the specified derived comparisons keep their mathematical meaning, while elaboration does not repeatedly reconstruct definitionally equal composite complex functors. Keep the module inverse image unchanged and record its additivity as a proved named instance; declare the iterated complex result type explicitly to avoid reconstructing the large inverse-image data during kernel conversion. The actual original-small-site construction, universal derived model, augmentation and pullback normalization are packaged by [def-sp-constant-reduction-models]; its public reexport preserves the original module API.

Write $\Delta_T$ for constant towers, $Q_T=(\underline{P_n}_T)_n$, and $i_{T,M}:\Delta_TM\to\mathcal R_T(M)$ for tensoring with the strict quotient map $\Delta_T\underline A_T\to Q_T$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] with the small category $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op}$ at all four corners. The termwise adjunction is an adjunction on diagrams: transposing the components of a tower map transposes its transition squares because the original hom-set bijection is natural. Hence it gives the stated diagram-topos morphisms and their commutative square. Tensor on these sites is termwise, since the presheaf tensor is termwise and the sheaf condition is imposed separately at every integer. Choose a single flat-term K-flat resolution $Q\to M$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Its diagonal is K-flat: tensoring it with an acyclic tower gives an acyclic complex at each level, so is acyclic by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. To compute tensor with just this one K-flat factor, resolve the coefficient diagram by a flat-term K-flat complex $S\to Q_T$. The cone of $\Delta Q\otimes S\to\Delta Q\otimes Q_T$ is $\Delta Q$ tensored with the acyclic cone of $S\to Q_T$, and is acyclic by the definition [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The two-K-flat computation in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] therefore represents $\mathcal R_T(M)$ by the actual tower $(Q\otimes_A\underline{P_n})_n$, including its quotient transitions. The pullback tensor comparisons, including those for evaluation, are the canonical comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. In particular $G_u\mathcal R_V(M)=\mathcal R_U(u^*M)$ under these comparisons. This constructs whole diagram objects and maps; it does not lift a family of derived level maps. In the original pro-etale implementation, quotient_comm follows by composing the constant-scalar naturality square with the coefficient projection square. The ordinary strict reduction functor is additive because each evaluation is scalar extension followed by scalar restriction, both additive. For reduction_exists, take the resolving class of homotopy-category objects represented by K-flat complexes with independent coefficient universes. K-flat resolutions give a quasi-isomorphism from this class to every homotopy object. On a quasi-isomorphism between such representatives, each scalar extension is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]; exact scalar restriction, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], preserves it. Evaluation detects quasi-isomorphisms of strict towers, so the homotopy reduction functor inverts the resolving-class quasi-isomorphisms. Apply [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] to obtain the left-derived functor and its counit, invertible on the chosen resolving class. This proves the stated existence and K-flat computation property without changing the reduction functor signature.

proof.text: The constant-tower functor preserves K-injectives. Indeed $J$ has terminal object $1$, and a map from a tower $N$ to $\Delta V$ is uniquely a map $N_1\to V$; hence $\operatorname{ev}_1\dashv\Delta$, with exact left adjoint by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. The small ordinary and diagram sites have K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. A K-injective representative $I$ of $M$ therefore gives $R_u^{\mathcal T}\Delta M=\Delta Ru_*M$ and $\mathcal L_T\Delta M=M$, since termwise $u_*\Delta I=\Delta u_*I$ and $\lim\Delta I=I$; the first assertion uses the K-injective computation [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], and the second [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. These are canonical natural identifications. The adjunction bijections on diagonal representatives are the original bijections termwise. The fraction characterization of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] consequently identifies their derived units and counits with the diagonals of the original derived ones. Thus the diagram mate on $\Delta K$ is $\Delta e$, where $e:g^*Rf_*K\to Rf'_*g'^*K$ is the ordinary derived mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Under the completion identification of [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction], $\mathcal L_T(i_{T,M}):M\to\mathcal L_T\mathcal R_T(M)$ is exactly the completion unit, denoted $j_{T,M}:M\to C_TM$.

proof.text: For each fixed n, form the finite counit mate [def-sp-constant-quotient-projection]. Apply mateEquiv_vcomp to the normalized reduction/pullback square and the inverse evaluation/pullback square. It identifies evaluation of projection followed by the canonical evaluation/direct-image comparison with this finite mate. The evaluation/direct-image comparison is invertible by [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations]. The single-quotient perfect projection theorem [lem-sp-constant-perfect-quotient-projection] therefore makes every evaluated projection invertible. To detect invertibility of the strict tower morphism, use DerivedCategory.isIso_iff. Exact evaluation commutes naturally with each homology functor; each component of the homology natural transformation is invertible, so NatIso.isIso_of_isIso_app makes the entire homology transformation invertible. This proves projection_isIso with a complete categorical argument. The finite perfect projection is the separate source lemma; no arbitrary comparison isomorphisms or equality-of-evaluated-morphisms criterion is introduced.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] to any of the constant-coefficient ringed-topos morphisms $u$. It supplies the canonical natural isomorphism $a_{u,N}:Ru_*\mathcal L_U N\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_V R_u^{\mathcal T}N$, induced by the identical underived composites $u_*\lim=\lim u_*^{\mathcal T}$. Its specified K-injective normalization commutes with tower projections. For $u=f'$ and $N=G_{g'}\mathcal R_XK=\mathcal R_{X'}(g'^*K)$ this is exactly $t$ in the statement, with all its evaluation identifications. For constant towers the comparisons in step 2 identify $a_{u,\Delta F}$ with the identity of $Ru_*F$: on a diagonal K-injective representative both composites are the same complex $u_*I$.

Put $M=g^*Rf_*K$, $E=g'^*K$, $N=Rf'_*E$, and let $e:M\to N$ be the ordinary mate. Set $H'=h_{f',E}:\mathcal R_{Y'}N\to R_{f'}^{\mathcal T}\mathcal R_{X'}E=D$, using step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] on the four small diagram sites with object $\Delta K$ and coefficient diagram $Q_Y$. For every edge, inverse image of the constant quotients and their quotient maps gives the required identification $G_uQ_V=Q_U$, compatible with the specified square. The first composite of the cited coherence statement is precisely $vH$; the second is $H'\mathcal R_{Y'}(e)$, because the exchange on $\Delta K$ is $\Delta e$ by step 2. Consequently
$$vH=H'\mathcal R_{Y'}(e)$$
in the derived diagram category itself, naturally in $K$. This is a direct instance of that node's two displayed composites; in particular it establishes equality before applying any limit or evaluation.

proof.text:
For any $u,F$, the naturality in the coefficient argument and the tensor-unit normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], applied on the diagram sites to $\Delta\underline A\to Q$, give
$$h_{u,F}\,i_{V,Ru_*F}=R_u^{\mathcal T}(i_{U,F}).$$
Indeed the projection for the tensor unit is $1_{\Delta Ru_*F}$, and the two vertical maps in this naturality square are exactly the displayed strict quotient-unit maps; no resolution of the quotient diagram is chosen separately at its levels. Define
$$\rho_{u,F}=a_{u,\mathcal R_UF}^{-1}\,\mathcal L_V(h_{u,F}):C_VRu_*F\longrightarrow Ru_*C_UF.$$
Apply $\mathcal L$ to the first equation and use the naturality of $a_u$ from [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] for the actual tower morphism $i_{U,F}$. Since $a_{u,\Delta F}=1$ and $\mathcal L(i_F)=j_F$ by steps 2 and 4, the result is the normalized unit equation
$$\rho_{u,F}\,j_{V,Ru_*F}=Ru_*(j_{U,F}).$$
This is a functorial equality derived from a square of diagram morphisms, not from its level evaluations.

proof.text:
Let $r=t^{-1}\mathcal L_{Y'}(v)s$. Apply $\mathcal L$ to the equality in step 5 and use $s=\mathcal L(H)$ with the specified completion identification. Steps 4 and 6 give
$$r=\rho_{f',E}\,C_{Y'}(e),\qquad
rj_{Y',M}=\rho_{f',E}j_{Y',N}e=Rf'_*(j_{X',E})e.$$
The middle equality is naturality of the completion unit. By [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction], $C_{X'}E$ and $Rf'_*C_{X'}E$ are complete; thus precomposition with $j_{Y',M}$ is a bijection from maps $C_{Y'}M\to Rf'_*C_{X'}E$ to maps $M\to Rf'_*C_{X'}E$. The last display characterizes $r$ uniquely.

proof.text:
We make the completed-square normalization explicit. For any edge $u$ and any ambient object $F$, the map $b_{u,F}=C_Uu^*(j_{V,F}):C_Uu^*F\to C_Uu^*C_VF$ is an isomorphism. To check this without assuming that inverse image preserves complete objects, test maps to a complete $L$: the two hom-set bijections of [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction] identify precomposition with $b_{u,F}$ with precomposition by $j_{V,F}$ on maps into the complete object $Ru_*L$, which is bijective. Taking $L$ successively to be the source and target constructs a two-sided inverse. Write $L=f^*$, $L'=f'^*$, $G=g^*$, $H_0=g'^*$, $R=Rf_*$, $R'=Rf'_*$. Let $\theta:L'G\to H_0L$ be the ordinary square comparison. On a complete object $W$ put
$$b_l=C_{X'}L'(j_{Y',GW}),\quad b_r=C_{X'}H_0(j_{X,LW}),\quad
\theta^c_W=b_r\,C_{X'}(\theta_W)\,b_l^{-1}.$$
Here is the hom-set calculation fixing this comparison. For two consecutive edges $u:U\to V$ and $v:Z\to U$, put $B_{v,u,W}=C_Zv^*(j_{U,u^*W})$. For complete $W$ on $V$ and complete $T$ on $Z$, the composite completed adjunction identifies
$$\operatorname{Hom}(C_Zv^*C_Uu^*W,T)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(v^*C_Uu^*W,T)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(C_Uu^*W,Rv_*T)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(u^*W,Rv_*T)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(W,Ru_*Rv_*T).$$
The third bijection is valid because $Rv_*T$ is complete. For $x:C_Zv^*C_Uu^*W\to T$, naturality of $j$ gives
$$xB_{v,u,W}j_{Z,v^*u^*W}
=xj_{Z,v^*C_Uu^*W}v^*(j_{U,u^*W}).$$
Under $v^*\dashv Rv_*$, precomposition by $v^*(j_{U,u^*W})$ becomes precomposition by $j_{U,u^*W}$. Thus the displayed completed hom-set chain sends $x$ to the ordinary composite transpose of $xB_{v,u,W}j_{Z,v^*u^*W}$. In particular $B_{v,u,W}^{-1}$ identifies the composite completed left adjoint with $C_Zv^*u^*$ while preserving this transpose. Apply this calculation first to $(u,v)=(g,f')$ and then to $(f,g')$. For every $x:C_{X'}H_0C_XLW\to T$ we obtain
$$x\theta^c_W b_l j_{X',L'GW}
=xb_r C_{X'}(\theta_W)j_{X',L'GW}
=xb_r j_{X',H_0LW}\theta_W.$$
Consequently precomposition with $\theta^c_W$ becomes exactly precomposition with the ordinary $\theta_W$ in the two ordinary composite adjunctions. The latter is conjugate to the prescribed right-adjoint square: the canonical comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] are induced by composition of the ordinary adjunction hom-set bijections. Their specified K-injective representatives, and the fraction formula of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general], identify these bijections with the derived composite ones. Their restrictions to complete objects have the same maps, because each direct image preserves completeness. The bijection of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] therefore identifies the displayed $\theta^c$ with exactly the conjugate required in the item. Likewise the completed counit $\varepsilon^c_K:C_XLRK\to K$ is the unique extension of the ordinary counit, so $\varepsilon^c_Kj_{X,LRK}=\varepsilon_K$, since $K$ is complete. These statements follow from the actual hom-set bijections, so they fix the maps as well as their isomorphism classes.

proof.text:
Now compute $E^c j_{Y',M}$ using [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Recall $M=GRK$ and $E=H_0K$. The transpose of $E^c$ under $C_{X'}L'\dashv R'$ is
$$\beta^c=C_{X'}H_0(\varepsilon^c_K)\,\theta^c_{RK}:C_{X'}L'C_{Y'}M\longrightarrow C_{X'}E.$$
Therefore the ordinary transpose of $E^c j_{Y',M}$ under $L'\dashv R'$ is $\beta^c j_{X',L'C_{Y'}M}L'(j_{Y',M})$. Naturality of $j$ identifies the final two factors with $b_lj_{X',L'M}$. Substitute step 8 and cancel $b_l^{-1}b_l$ to obtain
$$C_{X'}H_0(\varepsilon^c_K)\,b_r\,C_{X'}(\theta_{RK})\,j_{X',L'M}
=C_{X'}(H_0\varepsilon_K\,\theta_{RK})j_{X',L'M}
=j_{X',E}\,H_0\varepsilon_K\,\theta_{RK}.$$
Here the first equality uses $b_r=C_{X'}H_0(j_{X,LRK})$ and $\varepsilon^c_Kj_{X,LRK}=\varepsilon_K$; the second is naturality of $j$. The ordinary exchange transpose is $H_0\varepsilon_K\theta_{RK}$ by the cited mate definition, so the last expression is the transpose of $R'(j_{X',E})e$. The ordinary adjunction bijection gives
$$E^c j_{Y',M}=Rf'_*(j_{X',E})e.$$
Thus $E^c$ and $r$ have the same restriction along the completion unit. The bijection in step 7 proves $E^c=r$, and multiplication by $t$ proves the ordered identity in the item. Every operation used is a functor, a specified natural comparison, or a hom-set bijection natural in its variables. Hence the equality is an equality of natural transformations on the complete subcategory.

proof.text: It remains to check the asserted finite-coefficient normalization, independently of the equality just proved. Evaluation preserves K-injectives by [lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective], is exact by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], and has the direct-image comparison of [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]. With the pullback/tensor comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], evaluation of the unit--square--counit formula [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] is consequently the ordinary constant-$A$ exchange on $K\otimes_A^L\underline{P_n}$. To identify this with restriction of the $P_n$-coefficient mate, use the two factorizations of the same ringed-topos morphism $(U,\underline{P_n})\to(V,\underline A)$, through $(U,\underline A)$ and through $(V,\underline{P_n})$. The canonical composition comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] gives $\operatorname{Res}\,Ru_{*,P_n}\cong Ru_{*,A}\operatorname{Res}$, since scalar restriction is exact. Pullback comparison is the literal identity $\operatorname{Res}\,u^*_{P_n}=u^*_A\operatorname{Res}$ on complexes, because these are constant coefficients and inverse image is exact. For $P_n$-module sheaves, a map of underlying $A$-module sheaves is $P_n$-linear: the action of each local quotient section is locally the action of a lift in $\underline A$, since $\underline A\to\underline{P_n}$ is an epimorphism. Thus the module adjunction bijection $a:u^*M\to N\mapsto u_*a\circ\eta_M$ is unchanged on underlying modules. Its derived fraction characterization in [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] makes the displayed derived comparisons preserve the units and counits as well. The scalar square commutes, since every map sends $a\bmod I^n$ to its inverse-image section. Substitution into the mate formula therefore gives precisely the restriction of the ordinary $P_n$-coefficient mate. Here $K\otimes_A^L\underline{P_n}$ carries its canonical derived $P_n$-module structure through the strict flat representative $(Q\otimes_A\underline{P_n})$ of step 1. No flatness of $A\to P_n$, finite cardinality, geometric base-change theorem, or etale-origin witness has entered this calculation.

The statement, the ten-step proof and all the other fields were already in the base. I reviewed all of it in full. The setting (Noetherian A, perfect P_n=A/I^n, any square of topoi, constant-A coefficients, C=Rlim(-⊗P_n)) matches Stacks 099N (proetale.tex l.4336) and lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction. E^c is the mate for the completed adjunctions, its square comparison is fixed as the conjugate of the direct-image composition maps, and s and t are specified maps; this is exactly what parent fix-lem-exchanges Steps 3 and 9 use. The blueprint proof text is the same in master and main-20261015. Steps checked: S1 builds the strict tower (Q⊗P_n)_n from a single K-flat factor (the cone is ΔQ⊗acyclic). S2: since 1 is terminal, ev_1⊣Δ with ev_1 exact, so Δ preserves K-injectives, which gives R^TΔ=ΔRu_*, LimΔ=id, diagram mate Δe and L(i)=j. S3: the projection maps are isomorphisms through the strict-perfect package of the constant sheaves of a finite projective resolution, then levelwise. S4 is a direct instance of the pushforward/limit comparison (elementary). S5: exchange-tensor-coherence on the diagram sites gives vH=H'R(e) before any limit. S6: naturality in P and α_unit=1 give ρj=Ru_*(j). S7: r=ρC(e) and rj=Rf'_*(j_E)e, unique because Rf'_*C_{X'}E is complete. S8 (3098 chars): b_{u,F} is invertible by Yoneda, the composite completed hom chain checks, θ^c corresponds to θ, and ε^c j=ε. It is one fully written computation with no hidden lemma, so it may stay. S9: the transpose computation gives E^c j_M=R'(j_E)e, hence E^c=r and tE^c=L(v)s. S10 (2231 chars): evaluation of the mate formula plus the Res/κ comparisons and P_n-linearity through the local epimorphism. It is one argument, and lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients (étale D^+, forgetting to abelian sheaves) is a different statement, so it may stay. Edge cases checked: I=0, I=A, identity square, A=0; perfectness is necessary (A/I with A=k[x]/(x^2), I=(x) is not perfect). No cycle; the only citer is fix-lem-exchanges. Nearest nodes (lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange, lem-weil-pbc-strict-tower-exchange-mate-normalization) are different statements, not duplicates. lean.statement: abbrev completionMateComparison {Y X Y' X' : Site.{u}} {f : Morphism Y X} {g : Morphism Y Y'} {h : Morphism X X'} {k : Morphism Y' X'} (sq : Square f g h k) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) (_hperfect : PerfectQuotients A I) : (∀ K : X.Complete A I, IsIso (projectionComparison (f := f) (g := g) A I K.obj)) ∧ (∀ (K : X.Complete A I) (n : ℕ), (Y'.evaluate A n).map (projectionComparison (f := f) (g := g) A I K.obj) ≫ (finiteSourceIso (f := f) (g := g) A I n K.obj).hom = (Y'.finiteEvaluationIso A I n).hom.app ((g.pull A).obj ((f.push A).obj K.obj)) ≫ (Y'.finiteRestriction A I n).map (finiteProjectionComparison (f := f) (g := g) A I n K.obj)) ∧ (Functor.whiskerRight (completeExchange sq A I) (ObjectProperty.ι (Y'.IsComplete A I)) ≫ (comparisonT (h := h) (k := k) A I).hom = comparisonS (f := f) (g := g) A I ≫ Functor.whiskerRight (Functor.whiskerLeft (ObjectProperty.ι (X.IsComplete A I) ⋙ X.reduction A I) (towerExchange sq A)) (Y'.rlim A)) ∧ (∀ (K : X.Complete A I) (n : ℕ), (Y'.evaluate A n).map ((towerExchange sq A).app ((X.reduction A I).obj K.obj)) ≫ (finiteTargetIso (h := h) (k := k) A I n K.obj).hom = (finiteSourceIso (f := f) (g := g) A I n K.obj).hom ≫ (Y'.finiteRestriction A I n).map ((ordinaryExchange sq (quotientRing A I n)).app ((X.finiteReduction A I n).obj K.obj)))
